claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child I'm asking about - my son Alex. He's 7 years old, but he doesn't live with me at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I understand you have a son named Alex who is 7 years old and doesn't currently live with you.

To assess your eligibility, I need to understand more about your situation:

**Where does Alex currently live, and are you making any financial contributions towards his upkeep (such as for clothes, food, pocket money, or accommodation)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is currently in local authority care - he's been there for a couple of months now. But yes, I do still contribute towards his upkeep - I help out with about £50 a week for things like clothes and other bits he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. This is helpful for assessing your eligibility.

Just to clarify the timeline:

**You mentioned Alex has been in local authority care for a couple of months - is that more than 8 weeks, or less than 8 weeks?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been about 10 weeks now, so yes, more than 8 weeks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have a few more questions to complete my assessment:

**Does Alex spend any regular time at home with you - for example, does he come home for at least 24 hours a week, or spend 2 nights in a row each week, or 7 days or more in a row at home?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't come home regularly like that. He's at the care home full-time at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have one more important question:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.text:
**Assessment Complete**

Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to inform you that you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex at this time.

Here's why:

While Alex is 7 years old (which meets the age requirement) and you live in the UK, the issue is that Alex has been in local authority care for 10 weeks, which exceeds the 8-week limit. 

According to the Child Benefit rules, when a child is in local authority care for more than 8 weeks, you can only continue to receive Child Benefit if the child spends at least 24 hours a week at home with you. Since you've confirmed that Alex is at the care home full-time and doesn't come home regularly, this exception doesn't apply in your situation.

While I understand you're contributing £50 per week towards Alex's upkeep, this particular exception (regular spending) only applies to children in hospital or residential accommodation, not to children in local authority care.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future - for example, if he begins spending at least 24 hours per week at home, or 2 nights in a row each week, or 7 days or more in a row at home - you may be able to claim Child Benefit again at that point.
